original_question: Let tau = p/q, and let M_tau be the limb of the quadratic connectedness locus having interior angle p/q. Is the diameter of M_tau bounded above by K/q^2 for some constant K independent of tau? If not, is it at least bounded above by K log(q)/q^2?
target_in_paper: §1, "Local connectivity of Julia sets," specifically Question 12. The draft is targeting the paper's exact limb-diameter question, stated immediately after the paper introduces the quadratic connectedness locus and just after Question 11 identifies it with the Mandelbrot set. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object (the limb M_tau), the right parameterization (tau = p/q), and the exact two asymptotic bounds asked in the paper, namely K/q^2 and, failing that, K log(q)/q^2. It is very close to the wording of Question 12. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient family should be stated: P_c(z) = z^2 + c. The paper asks this inside the quadratic family, not for a general connectedness locus. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The "connectedness locus" should be identified explicitly as the set of parameters c for which the Julia set of P_c is connected; in Question 11 the paper also calls this the quadratic connectedness locus, i.e. the Mandelbrot set. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

To make the notation stand-alone, tau = p/q should be specified as a rational interior angle, typically taken in lowest terms with q >= 2; the paper leaves the reduction convention implicit when it writes "Let tau = p/q." ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The diameter should be understood as the Euclidean diameter of the subset M_tau in the parameter c-plane; the paper leaves the metric ambient space implicit. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

The quantifier should be made explicit: the question is whether there exists a universal constant K > 0 independent of tau and valid for every rational tau of the form p/q. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

A nearby paper-faithful contextual remark is omitted: the still-unpublished Yoccoz inequality is said to give the weaker bound diam(M_tau) = O(1/q). This is not part of the question itself, but it helps locate the intended sharpness. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
refined_question: For the quadratic family P_c(z) = z^2 + c, let M be the quadratic connectedness locus (the Mandelbrot set), and for a reduced rational interior angle tau = p/q let M_tau denote the limb of M with interior angle p/q. Does there exist a universal constant K > 0, independent of tau, such that diam(M_tau) < K/q^2 for every tau? If not, does there at least exist a universal constant K > 0 such that diam(M_tau) < K log(q)/q^2 for every tau?
justification: This is Question 12 in §1 almost verbatim. On the preceding page the paper restricts to the quadratic family P_c(z) = z^2 + c with c ranging over parameters for which the Julia set is connected, and Question 11 explicitly identifies the resulting quadratic connectedness locus with the Mandelbrot set. Question 12 then introduces tau = p/q and M_tau as the limb with interior angle p/q and asks exactly whether its diameter is less than K/q^2, or failing that less than K log(q)/q^2. The only paper-nearby additional context is the remark that the unpublished Yoccoz inequality gives the weaker O(1/q) bound. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))
